answer.rationale:
Audit note applying to all six: each is a consolidated summary with the source archived, so none carries effect size, sample size, duration, confidence interval, or segment definition, and none can be re-inspected. Every rating is therefore capped — nothing here rises to 5. I graded on one question: how close does the stated outcome sit to sustainable long-term qualified revenue?

memory_57 (4): the only memory that names qualified revenue directly AND reports a durability check (retention). 'No measurable harm' is a null result of unknown power, and referrals in established customers may partly cannibalize revenue that would have arrived anyway, so not a 5 — but it is the closest thing to on-objective evidence in the set.

memory_44 (3): pipeline quality is a genuine qualified-revenue proxy, one step from the objective. Silent on close rates, CAC of a sales-assisted motion, and whether pipeline converted — so directionally useful, not conclusive.

memory_31 (2): first-week activation is a distant proxy. 'Durable' is asserted without a stated window. Critically, removing signup fields can raise activation counts while lowering lead qualification — the exact axis the objective cares about — and the memory is silent on downstream revenue.

memory_73 (2): reports acquisition and revenue lift but omits margin, discount depth, cohort retention, and post-promotion renewal. Discount-acquired SMB cohorts are the classic case where short-term revenue and sustainable revenue diverge. This memory is the most tempting match to today's competitor-pricing pressure and the least equipped to justify that match — high salience, low support.

memory_86 (2): completion rate and time-to-value are process metrics; 'early product adoption' is still upstream of revenue. No retention or expansion data.

memory_91 (1, least supported): week-one engagement and 'first meaningful action' are the shallowest proxies in the set — one short-term behavioral nudge, no revenue, no retention, no durability window, and 'meaningful action' is undefined. It is the furthest from the objective and the easiest to move without moving anything that matters.

Standing caution for this cycle: the two current declines (activation -6%, onboarding -4%) pattern-match to memory_31/86/91, and the competitor threat pattern-matches to memory_73. That match is a retrieval artifact, not evidence — those are precisely the memories whose recorded outcomes stop short of revenue. The memory set is systematically biased toward easily-measured near-term proxies, so it will tend to recommend proxy-moving experiments regardless of the objective. Whatever experiment I select should be instrumented for qualified revenue and cohort retention, not just the proxy that triggered it.
